answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a deposit before earning reputation. When an agent vouches for another, part of its stake is exposed to slashing if that identity is later proven fraudulent. A fable of cheap personas then fails: each one needs capital, and colluding identities risk losing it. The cost is funds tied up and potential forfeiture. A kernel can record stakes and disputes, while a bridge from reputation to collateral rewards careful endorsements.
